prompt: Challenge C144-CH2: Downstream purification — specifically the ultrafiltration step — runs at only 55% of nominal throughput because the membranes foul with res

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Continuous enzymatic saccharification in membrane bioreactors with 10 kDa ultrafiltration modules has been demonstrated to maintain acceptable flux over extended operation through daily backwash protocols, achieving 87–92% enzyme retention and steady-state operation for 14 days.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03519","field":"abstract","quote":"10 kDa cutoff hollow-fibre ultrafiltration module was evaluated for continuous enzymatic saccharification with enzyme recycle. Pre-treated wheat straw (organosolv, 60% EtOH, 160 °C) was fed as a 10% (w/v) suspension. Membrane fouling was characterised by trans-membrane pressure increase; a daily 15 min backwash protocol maintained acceptable flux over the operating period."}]},{"text":"Polyethersulfone ultrafiltration membranes fouled with biomass-rich process streams can be recovered to 93.1–97.4% of original water flux using alkaline cleaning protocols, with trade-offs between flux recovery speed and membrane lifetime preservation.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03378","field":"abstract","quote":"polyethersulphone and ceramic ultrafiltration membranes fouled with skim milk and cottage cheese whey streams. Protocol B achieved the highest PWFR of 97.4% for polyethersulphone membranes but reduced membrane lifetime by approximately 18% after 30 cleaning cycles. Protocol C preserved membrane integrity better and achieved PWFR of 93.1%."}]},{"text":"High-solids enzymatic hydrolysis processes require attention to slurry rheology evolution and mixing characteristics, and enzyme recycling via ultrafiltration membranes presents both technical and economic considerations for bioprocess scale-up.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03514","field":"abstract","quote":"mass transfer limitations, rheology of high-solids slurries, reactor configurations (stirred tank, horizontal drum, and oscillatory flow reactors), and strategies for fed-batch substrate addition. The chapter also covers enzyme recycling options — ultrafiltration membrane recycle and magnetic particle immobilisation — and their techno-economic implications."}]}],"fit":"partial","fitReason":"The researcher has direct experimental experience with 10 kDa polyethersulfone ultrafiltration fouling and maintenance in enzyme recycling systems [SYN-PUB-03519], and knowledge of CIP protocols for biomass-fouled membranes [SYN-PUB-03378], but the publications focus on saccharification processes rather than protease downstream purification, and do not address pre-filtration optimization or residual cell debris characterization in non-enzymatic bioprocesses."}
